html:
SMTO-UI-0036 — This value needs at least one named item

GUID: 833fa5f4-e336-4ee5-b758-40d2bf8d122c
Slug: ui-json-object-required
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • A saved value is stored as one or more named items, like a name followed by its value. What you typed had no named items, so the parameter wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. On the Value tab, write each item as a name and a value inside curly braces, for example {"username": "maria", "password": "your password"}. SMTO stores a parameter's value as named items so the Agent knows what each part is.
  2. If the value is just one piece of text, such as a single key or a note, select FREE FORM above the value box and type it as ordinary text. Free form saves plain text without needing names and braces.
  3. Select Save at the top of the parameter. Nothing is stored until the value is in an accepted form and you save.

What success looks like

  • The parameter shows "Saved" and the error under the value box is gone.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste your real password or key into the message you send them.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Parameter Store value editor (JSON mode) requires a non-empty JSON object, but the text parsed to null, an array, a scalar or an empty object {}.

What this means

  • An object-designated parameter parses to null, an array, another type or an empty object. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • An object-designated parameter parses to null, an array, another type or an empty object.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the parsed type and object keys without exposing secret values.

How to fix it

  • parameter_editor.js parseJson(valueEditor, "Value") throws ui_json_object_required when value_json is not a non-empty object. Enter an object such as {"token": "..."}, or switch the value to FREE FORM, which stores {"free_form_text": ...}.
  • Enter a nonempty JSON object in the marked field.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A nonempty supported JSON object passes validation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
